Memory.Authorization.Explanation: System optimization requires administrator rights. Once requests UAC for this run. Authorize future runs installs on-demand tasks limited to fixed memory operations; AF keeps normal privileges. Revoke them in settings. Automation requires this authorization.
Memory.Authorization.Missing: Not authorized; one-time approval is available
Memory.Authorization.NeedsRepair: Authorization mismatch; authorize again to repair
Memory.Authorization.Ready: Authorized; fixed tasks are ready on demand
Memory.Authorization.Revoked: System optimization authorization for this installation was revoked
Memory.Authorization.Title: System optimization authorization
Memory.Auto.Description: Runs while AF is open, awake and unlocked. The threshold must persist for 30 seconds. Attempts have a 15-minute cooldown; threshold triggers rearm after a 5-point drop. No success notifications.
Memory.Auto.Paused: Paused after authorization loss or repeated failures; check the latest result before resuming
Memory.Auto.Title: Automatic system optimization
Memory.Deep.Description: Collect unused objects and try to return AF physical memory. Later use may briefly stall.
Memory.Explanation: These counters overlap and must not be added. Deep reclaim may increase later page faults; a lower reading does not prove a leak is fixed.
Memory.Gentle.Description: Collect unused objects while keeping resident pages to reduce stalls on later use.

Memory.System.DeepDescription: Trim the system file cache working set and clear all standby pages. Later access may rebuild caches.
Memory.System.Description: Standard clears low-priority standby pages; Deep also processes the system file cache and all standby pages. Requires administrator approval. Caches may need rebuilding; support and effects vary by Windows version.
Memory.System.PartialSuccess: Some operations completed; see individual results
Memory.System.PermissionDenied: Permission denied; cleanup was not performed
Memory.System.ResultExplanation: Standby pages already count as available memory, so clearing cache may not lower memory usage. Readings include other programs’ activity. Successful execution does not guarantee improved performance; caches may rebuild afterward.
Memory.System.Scope: Standard clears low-priority standby pages. Deep also trims the system file cache and clears all standby pages, without trimming other applications.
Memory.System.TimedOut: Timed out; result unconfirmed. No automatic retry.
Memory.System.Title: System memory optimization
Memory.System.Unsupported: This cleanup operation is unsupported here

Start.Description: Learn the media bar and find settings for common tasks.
Start.Development.Body: This local build includes section navigation, Quick start and task-based settings pages. These interface changes are separate from the published 1.6 release notes.
Start.Faq.Customization: What should I know about third-party customization tools?
Start.Faq.Customization.Body: Apart from the compatible TranslucentTB, other customization tools, especially those that modify or replace the native taskbar, have not been thoroughly tested. Layout conflicts or unavailable features may occur. We recommend desktop floating mode when using these tools. If you encounter problems, please report the tool name, version and steps to reproduce.
Start.Faq.Lyrics.Body: Check enabled lyric sources, connectivity and track metadata. Some tracks have no available lyrics. Disabled online sources are not queried.
Start.Faq.Smtc: Playback controls do not work, or artwork is missing?
Start.Faq.Smtc.Body: Try enabling SMTC, system media control support, or system playback controls in the player settings, then start playback again. The option name varies by player.
Start.Faq.Source.Body: Start playback, then check the selected source and allow list. Players without a system media session or dedicated integration may not be discovered.
Start.Full.Description: Use the expand entry to open artwork, lyrics and other panel regions.
Start.History.Description: The following comes from the local cache or bundled catalogue. Open Update highlights for the complete history.
Start.Hover.Description: Hover over the media bar to reveal playback buttons. Choose which buttons appear and adjust their size and spacing.
Start.Intro.Description: See what is playing at rest, use controls on hover, and open the full panel for more detail. All layers share appearance and feature settings.
Start.Players.Note: Capabilities depend on player version and session. SMTC is the Windows system media session; missing controls or timeline data remain unavailable. This table describes integrations, not validation of every version.
Start.Release16.Body:
Audio device management and switching shortcuts are now available, with aliases and ordering.
Floating mode supports collapse at all four edges; vertical display follows the system taskbar orientation.
The full-panel entry opens on click or hover. Bluetooth battery remains an experiment, off by default.
Start.Rest.Description: Choose artwork, text and components, their order, and what stays visible without media.
Start.Runtime.Body: Requires Windows 10 1809 or later, x64, and Microsoft Edge WebView2 Evergreen Runtime. Release packages include .NET; ordinary build output may require a separate runtime.
Start.Tutorial.Daily.Body:
Configure click and wheel actions in Interaction & shortcuts.
Drag the handle on the right to reorder a list. Press Esc to cancel a drag.
Press Ctrl + F to search. Related links appear when a row is hovered or contains keyboard focus.
Start.Tutorial.Daily.Short: Clicks, wheel gestures, shortcuts and drag handles.
Start.Tutorial.Devices.Body:
1. Enable, rename and order devices in Audio devices.
2. Show input or output buttons in At rest.
3. Configure device shortcuts and action targets in Interaction & shortcuts. Bluetooth battery requires its experiment and data supplied by Windows and the driver.
Start.Tutorial.Devices.Short: Manage input and output devices, then choose their media-bar entries.
Start.Tutorial.Lyrics.Body:
1. Adjust title, artist and lyric layout in Text & lyrics.
2. Set two-line lyrics, secondary lines and word timing in Lyric display.
3. Enable and order lyric sources. Online searches send track and artist information; disable sources you do not need.
Start.Tutorial.Lyrics.Short: Adjust media text, lyric presentation and lyric sources.
Start.Tutorial.Mode.Body:
1. Choose the mode and monitor in Display & position.
2. Taskbar mode follows the system taskbar. Vertical display requires a taskbar on the left or right edge.
3. In floating mode, adjust position, orientation and edge collapse. Geometry is stored separately for each mode.
Start.Tutorial.Mode.Short: Choose taskbar or floating mode, then set its position.
Start.Tutorial.Playback.Body:
1. Start a track in a supported player.
2. If several sources are available, select the application in the media-source menu.
3. Configure automatic switching, preferred apps and the allow list in Media sources. Controls and timeline support depend on the player.
Start.Tutorial.Playback.Short: Start playback in a player, then select its source.
